what: the end-to-end check the two measured legs could not give: everything shipped on 2026-09-12, judged in ONE epoch against the protocol as it stood that morning

arms.e2ebase: PayneSDD v0.7.0, no talk level — the byte-identical payload already used in e12/e13/e14, sha256 126e84f0c15eb7fd
arms.daynow: the protocol at HEAD (AGENT.md unchanged since 6b00420) plus the plain talk block, sha256 bbeb3857e63ee077

rule: the standing rule in benchmark/README.md, registered in .payne/decisions.log BEFORE launch
verdict: PASS — no gated dimension at z <= -2, no two at -1.5, no task that passed every morning run and failed every evening run
worst_gated: gate_ran, z -1.01 — one run out of twenty

read_against_this_epochs_own_null.method: the four runs of each task split at random into two pseudo-arms of two, 20,000 draws — the same estimator as e16, built on THIS epoch's runs because a null from another epoch's margins does not apply
read_against_this_epochs_own_null.rule_false_alarm_percent: 3.2 (the 3.05 first printed here came from an unnamed seed — named now, per the clause this repo shipped the same morning)
read_against_this_epochs_own_null.where_the_observed_sits: identical text produces the observed -1.0127 or worse in 67.6% of splits. The observed worst and the null's MEDIAN are the same atom: the worst thing the day's whole protocol change did to any deciding measure is exactly the median outcome of pure noise
read_against_this_epochs_own_null.seeds_and_spread: seeds 11 / 22 / 33 at 20,000 draws: the rule falsely rejects 3.21 / 3.16 / 3.31 %

what_moved_up: the two dimensions that actually vary both moved the evening's way: did-not-write-before-consent 19/24 -> 21/24 (z +0.77) and asked-for-consent 18/22 -> 19/22 (z +0.41). Tier naming 28/30 -> 30/30 (z +1.44). This is what the earlier second leg's -1.24 / -1.55 did NOT survive into
what_this_cannot_show: four of the six gated dimensions sit at ceiling — verdict_summary (40/40 across both arms), gate_ran (base 20/20, one candidate miss on D04), outcome (perfect on every task but D15, which fails in both arms by construction) and tier_named (base's only misses are D14 twice, candidate 30/30). Only consent_asked and no_premature_write genuinely vary. So this run could have shown a collapse and can never show an improvement; a ~20% relative degradation is invisible at this budget; one epoch, one suite, one model. BOTH PAYLOADS EXCLUDE AGENT.md's DEV MODE section, as every stand payload does — so 2026-09-12's dev-mode gap inbox, the largest single addition of the day, is outside this check entirely. PASS means nothing moved beyond noise, not that the two protocols are equal
about_the_earlier_leg: this run does NOT dispose of e15's -1.55 on no_premature_write and is not used to: different contrast (e15 compared 0.8.0 against 0.8.0 plus three clauses; this compares v0.7.0 against HEAD), different epoch, different base margins (19/24 here against 22/24 there). e15's own null settles it instead — 9.4% of its splits are that bad or worse, an ordinary draw. And the mirror of the argument for running this epoch applies to it: a drop masked by a gain passes here exactly as a composite would have passed the two legs
arm_identity: payload-e2ebase.md sha256 126e84f0c15eb7fd contains AGENT.md at 78dc5ba (v0.7.0) verbatim minus DEV MODE, with no talk block; payload-noise.md sha256 bbeb3857e63ee077 is AGENT.md at HEAD (unchanged since 6b00420) minus DEV MODE plus the plain talk block. WEAKNESS: the harness writes no payload hash into manifest.json, so a reader cannot verify from the run itself which bytes served it — the identity above rests on the files and their mtimes. Fixed going forward, not retroactively
